code_first.q: Predict the CPU register printed from a zero-indexed array.
p: Explain what the PC and MAR actually store; name the search algorithm that works without sorting.
code_first.a: Index 2 prints PC; index 0 prints MAR. PC holds the next instruction address; MAR holds the address being accessed. Linear search can inspect an unsorted array. This array-access example is not itself a complete search.

original_exam_questions: A linear search seeks 7 in [3,5,7,9]. Give number of checks. [2 marks]
State a requirement of binary search. [1 mark]
Explain what one pass of bubble sort guarantees. [3 marks]
After a full ascending pass, the largest unsorted value has reached the right end of that section.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: Array indexes begin at 0: MAR is index 0, MDR index 1, PC index 2.

stretch.task: Add a linear-search loop that finds MAR in the register-name array and prints its zero-based index.
stretch.hint: Loop through indexes 0 to 2; compare each register string to MAR.
stretch.answer: MAR occurs at index 0. A complete search should also handle a target that is not found.

mastery.task: Compare linear and binary search code on sorted [2,5,8,11,14,17,20] for target17; trace indexes and describe precondition.
mastery.hint: Linear visits indexes0..5; binary uses midpoint and halves.
mastery.answer: Linear six comparisons; binary mid3=11,low4; mid5=17 found in two comparisons.
